chunks: 1814 - And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said:
I was with my father while I was a boy, and we had dinner with al-Riḍā عليه السلام on the night of the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.

So he said to him: 'On the night of the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, Ibrāhīm عليه السلام was born, and on it ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام was born, and on it the earth was spread out from beneath the Kaʿbah. So whoever fasts that day is like one who has fasted sixty months.'

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ: Ibrāhīm; the prophet whose birth is mentioned
key_terms.دُحِيَتِ: was spread out; referring to the earth being spread from beneath the Kaʿbah
key_terms.ذِي ٱلْقَعْدَةِ: Dhū al-Qaʿdah; the lunar month in which this virtuous day occurs
key_terms.صَامَ: fasted; the devotional act for which the reward is described
key_terms.عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ: ʿĪsā son of Maryam; the prophet whose birth is also mentioned
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ: the night; the sacred date being identified in the report
key_terms.وُلِدَ: was born; indicating the births of revered prophets on this date
key_terms.ٱلْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah; the sacred center from beneath which the earth was spread

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah?
ai.summary: This hadith mentions the virtue of the twenty-fifth of Dhū al-Qaʿdah and connects it with significant sacred events, including the births of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام, and the spreading out of the earth from beneath the Kaʿbah. It also states the great reward for fasting on that day, equating it to fasting for sixty months.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1814 - It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:
‘I was with my father when I was a boy, and we had dinner with Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) on the night of the 25th of Dhu al-Qa‘dah.’
Imam (as) said to him: 'The 25th night of Dhu al-Qa‘dah is the night on which Ibrahim (as) was born, and on which Isa ibn Maryam (as) was born, and it is the night when the earth was spread out from beneath the Ka‘bah. Whoever fasts on that day, it is as if he has fasted for sixty months.'"
